text: Everything inside Data Factory Studio is organized behind five icons running down the left side of the screen. This lesson tours the two you'll actually spend the most time in early on: Author and Monitor.

Home is the landing page with quick shortcuts. Author, the pencil icon, is where you actually build pipelines, datasets, and data flows. Monitor, the speedometer, is where you watch every pipeline run. Manage, the briefcase, holds linked services, integration runtimes, and triggers. And Learning center offers guided tutorials and templates.

Selecting Author opens the hub where nearly all hands-on work in this course actually happens. Factory Resources, on the far left, is the tree of everything you've built — every pipeline, dataset, and data flow, all in one place. Select any pipeline to open its canvas, where activities from the middle pane get dragged in and wired together.

Select a dataset in Factory Resources, and its editor opens with a Connection tab, right here. This makes Lesson 1's dataset concept concrete: the linked service at the top says how to connect, and this tab says which specific data, inside that connection, this dataset actually points to — here, split into container, folder, and file name.

Selecting Monitor shows every pipeline run, triggered or debug, past or currently in progress — status, duration, and exactly what triggered it, all at a glance. Chapter 8 comes back to this hub in real depth.

Select a pipeline name from that list, and you see the actual activities that ran, in order, with a status icon on each one. Select the Details icon on any activity run for a full breakdown — for a Copy activity, that includes exactly how much data was read and written. This is exactly where you'll go the moment something in a real pipeline doesn't behave the way you expected.

Five hubs, and you now know what each one is actually for. Chapter 1 is complete. Next, Chapter 2 gets properly hands-on with connecting to real data — linked services and datasets, in depth, starting with Lesson 6.
